After the igniter of our Samsung oven broke, we initially ordered a non-OEM igniter which was considerably cheaper than the authentic part. It worked only for a month unfortunately. This one has been working better and heats up faster as well. While it is not super easy to install, if you are a little handy, it is installed in about one hour with the help of some videos you can easily find on youtube.

Oven wasn't heating up as quickly as it use too and I could hear it trying to reignite almost constantly (like a flame was coming in and out). It took a good 20-30 min to get to 350. During the install I saw the igniter appeared half charred. So maybe that was a good visual indicator? Who knows! You can't tell till you pull it out anyways. All I know is after the install my oven reached 350 at around 5-6 min and no more constant unexpected reignitions.  The only other thing I can comment on was that you may need an impact screw driver and/or a torch to get some screws out (only way I was able to remove 3/5 screws) , but please make sure you turn off the gas line and evacuate what is left before attempting.

I replaced it and oven fired right up.

Had for almost a week and have done a number of loads. The tub holds a good amount of clothes being that there is no upright agitator to take up room. One load consisted of...4 pr of pj bottoms. Two of which were the very thick fuzzy ones, 4 t-shirts, 6 pr socks, 6 pr undies and 2 pillow cases. Second load consisted of 2 queen size sheets, 2 pillow cases and 1 thinner bath towel. My clothes are adult large. My only con would be the hoses. Not very durable looking so I'll see how long they last. Trick I learned for the hose that attaches to the fawcet. Some people were saying they were having a difficult time getting it to fit. I ran hot water over it (from the fawcet) which made it more pliable to fit snugly over the fawcet. Also if you lay a damp dish rag over the sinks edge, it will keep the drain hose from slipping out of the sink. I have had no problems with lint as some people were stating. I've had the washer about a month and love it! I does a weeks worth of laundry in around two loads. The spin dry gets items very dry. I like the option to rinse and spin at the same time, the manual does not talk about it, but the hole that says rinse water inlet allows you to run water through the clothes while spinning and it saves so much time! I do my wash then fill the spinner with clothes, switch the hose to the spinner side, turn on the water, then set the spin for 5 min. I run the rinse water the first two min then turn it off and let the clothes spin for the last three min. Using this method a week of laundry is done and hung to dry in only 30 min. That's faster than one load in my apartment buildings shared machines and I don't have to walk up and down the five flights. As someone who needed a machine that required no plumbing attachments or sink attachments, I was delighted to learn of this machine from an acquaintance. I ordered the new larger version, hoping it would spare me trips to the laundromat. Alas, the basic flaw of this machine is the small water inlet holes and the cheap and very narrow plastic tube that is supposed to fit over the sink faucet. I have wider faucets than most, and have to fill the machine with a bucket as the plastic attachment does not work with my bathroom or kitchen faucets. The machine is also rather heavy to shift as it is larger than the older version. For some reason the drain hose comes up from the side rather than the back of the unit, essentially shortening its length. I have to hold the drain hose in place over my sink as it barely reaches over the wide lip of my kitchen sink. In brief, using this machine is almost more trouble than it is worth. It also requires a bucket or something low to the ground to let excess water drain from the machine to prevent leaking after you have supposedly drained all of the water out of the machine. The machine would be greatly improved by longer rubber hoses with flexible attachments to go over various sink faucets, and by larger inlet holes.

BASIC SETUP:
The initial setup is VERY intuitive, and only took us a few minutes to get started for our first load.
There is a standard three prong outlet plug, a hose which perfectly fit our sink to add water, and a drain hose which hooked over the side of our bathtub.

I've only had my panda XBP45 for less than 6 hours and already it has successfully done 6 loads of washing. Do not let this systems size put you off as it can easily hold 4 towels, couple pairs of jeans and other garments in the same wash. Couple of things I have noticed...

1. Do NOT over fill the spin section. I washed a full set of queen sheets and placed them both in the spin. The Panda spun them well but I noticed a table spoon of water under the machine. Upon closer inspection I noticed what appear to be drainage holes under the machine. The second time I spun those sheets I did them one at a time and no further leaks have appeared.

2. If you are someone living in an apartment that does not allow washers I can assure you the packaging for this machine has the word Panda stamped on the front of the box. Unless your landlord is aware what that could mean you should have no problems.

3. While this machine is fairly quiet the spin cycle is a little on the noisy side. I would imagine living in a ground floor apartment you would get away with running this machine without upsetting your neighbors. However on other levels of an apartment you will almost certainly alert the neighbors to the fact that you have a washing machine going.

I live in a small two-bedroom apartment in a city and was so tired of having to go to the laundromat as I had done for over four years. Enter the Panda Small Compact Portable Washing Machine. There are some great videos of other Panda washers here on Amazon. I recommend taking a look at those, particularly the one of this model's smaller size.

This little unit is fantastic. I've now used it a couple dozen times and it works great. With the spin dryer, your clothes will come out significantly drier than they would out of a washer--there will be no dripping and you can place your clothes on a rack and they'll be more or less dry in 12-24 hours in the summer (I keep mine in the bathtub and luckily have a window right there). So it's a bit more work, takes a bit more involvement, but did I mention it will save you from trips to the laundromat?

You'll want to use less soap and a little fabric softener. Your clothes won't be as soft and fluffy as they would if you used a regular dryer, but again, it's a cost and benefit analysis here: more expensive, mind-numbing trips to the laundromat or clothes that are air dried? If you have space and can afford it, perhaps the Panda dryer or something similar would be a great option, but I haven't tried it. This works just fine for my needs.

You'll also want to clean that lint catcher after washing, particularly if you have a pet. Also, I put mine in my bathroom and just put the water outlet hose in the bathtub

I ordered this on a Friday morning and got it Saturday night. Turn around was excellent. I only recently learned that portable washers existed! So I had to get one.Ok now about the machine.

When I got it, I was excited to use it. And use it I did. I did many loads of laundry that night, and even the extra work of filling the tub manually didn't really bother me. I felt accomplished.

I watched many videos of use for this unit (as well as others in the Panda line) and I knew that I should take it easy on loading the tub up. I keep loads small and I don't overload the spin dry side. You must treat this unit with care. Don't slam the lids down, especially the spin dry side. There is a clamp attached to a spring that will act as a break for the spin dry tub, and slamming the lid down could cause damage to that spring and clamp.

As for the spin dry side, I did encounter a problem that worried me. I heard an odd noise and I stopped the spin. I took the clothes out and then... The spin dry tub didn't spin anymore. Panic ensued. I've had this for one night, it can't be broken! Luckily, it wasn't broken. I had simply spin dried multiple clothes for too long and the motor overheated. I let it cool down and it works again. So, please do not use the spin dry side longer than is necessary! The spin tub is efficient and a couple minutes is fine. This was the only negative part about this machine, and why I decided on a four star rating
